Roaming and Map Pressure

Leaving your lane to help elsewhere can win games, or throw away your lead. Learn when to roam, how to do it, and what to do when your opponent disappears.

What roaming is

Roaming means leaving your lane to help another part of the map: ganking a lane, helping your jungler fight, or taking an objective. A good roam turns your lane advantage into kills and objectives for your whole team.

But every roam has a cost. While you're away, you're not getting minions or experience, and your opponent might be taking your tower plates. The goal is to roam when the reward is bigger than what you lose.

Push first, then roam

The golden rule of roaming: crash your wave before you leave. When you push the wave into the enemy tower, your opponent has two bad choices:

  • Stay and clear the wave under their tower, so they can't follow you.
  • Follow you and lose the whole wave (and maybe plates) to their tower.

If you roam with the wave pushing toward you, your opponent can push it into your tower, take plates and follow you anyway. Since plates are permanent now, that gold lead stays with them all game.

Pro tipPush, then roam through the river, not straight down the lane where the enemy can see you leave. The longer they don't notice you're gone, the better the gank works.

When to roam

Look for these good roaming moments:

  • A side lane is pushed up with no escape, especially if the enemy is low on health or used Flash.
  • Your jungler is fighting near your lane, like a scuttle crab fight or an invade.
  • An objective is about to spawn and your team needs numbers.
  • Your opponent just recalled or died, so they can't follow you.

Different roles roam differently. Mid laners are closest to both side lanes, so they roam the most. Supports often leave bot lane after the first recall to place vision and help mid. Top laners can roam with Teleport, and the top role quest now gives every top laner a free Unleashed Teleport later in the lane.

The cost of roaming

A roam is only good if it's worth more than what you lose. Be honest about the cost:

  • Lost minions and experience. A full wave early is worth over 100 gold and a lot of experience.
  • Turret plates. If your opponent shoves your tower while you're gone, they get plate gold.
  • The off-lane penalty early on. Farming minions outside your assigned lane before level 3 gives 25% less gold and experience, so stealing farm in another lane early isn't worth much.
Common mistakeRoaming without a plan and walking back with nothing. A failed roam that costs you two waves puts you behind your opponent in lane.

When your opponent roams

If your lane opponent disappears, do two things right away:

  1. Ping it. Use the "Enemy Missing" ping so your team knows. Do it quickly: a roam takes only 10-15 seconds to reach a side lane.
  2. Punish it. Push their wave into the tower, take plates, or follow them if you're stronger. You can also move to the same lane to help.

Many players do neither: they keep farming and the roaming player gets a free kill. If you can't stop the roam, make it cost them as much as possible.

Roaming as a support

Supports have a unique roaming role. After the first recall, a support can leave the ADC for a short time to:

  • Place deep wards in the enemy jungle.
  • Help mid gank or fight for the scuttle crab.
  • Group with the jungler before an objective.

Only do this when your ADC is safe: when the wave is pushed or near your tower, and the enemy bot lane isn't strong enough to dive. See Support.

Key takeaways

  • Crash your wave before you roam so your opponent can't follow for free.
  • Roam when there's a clear target: a pushed lane, a jungle fight, or an objective.
  • Every roam costs minions, experience and maybe plates. Make it worth it.
  • When your opponent goes missing, ping it and punish it.
  • Supports can roam after the first recall when the ADC is safe.
